descriptionChirho: A cheap, acidic wine commonly drunk by Roman soldiers; offered to Jesus on the cross (Matt 27:48, Mark 15:36, Luke 23:36, John 19:29-30). All six NT occurrences refer to the same substance in the Passion narrative, with the two sense clusters differing only in case form (genitive vs accusative). Multilingual evidence: spa vinagre, hin सिरका/सिरके 'vinegar', arb خَلّ 'vinegar', kor 식초/초 'vinegar', swa siki 'vinegar/sour liquid' — uniformly identifying an inexpensive sour wine rather than modern culinary vinegar.
